data.body:
CORRECTION to this ticket's description (the description itself could not be amended without invalidating the signed plan-review attestation, so the record is corrected here).

The description states that tests/unit/test_guides.py 'couples the guides to coach_moves.MOVE_REGISTRY only'. That is WRONG, and the plan reviewer correctly refuted it (advisory E4). test_guides.py imports explain_criterion from the registry and already contains five G6-specific parity tests at lines 99-180, added by the 828a fix: test_g6_still_forbids_requiring_rejected_alternatives, test_guide_does_not_instruct_authors_to_name_a_rejected_alternative, test_worked_example_models_a_single_approach, test_guide_still_requires_a_positive_rationale, and test_weigh_alternatives_coaching_move_is_unchanged.

The gap this ticket closes is therefore NARROWER than the description implies, but it is real and it is a class gap rather than an instance gap:

- Those five tests are hand-written, bespoke to ONE criterion (G6) and ONE claim (anti-priming). They exist only because a human found the 828a drift after it had shipped for a month.
- The plan guide cites 20 criteria. The other 19 had no coupling of any kind, and any citation added tomorrow would get none automatically.

So the 828a tests and this pin gate are COMPLEMENTARY, not redundant: the 828a tests assert the semantic content of one specific claim (something a digest pin cannot do), while the pin gate is the systematic net that makes ANY cited criterion's text change visible. Neither subsumes the other. The 828a tests were left untouched by this change and still pass.

Verified during implementation: with the pin gate absent, appending a contradictory rule to plan_review_F1.md (F1 is cited three times in the plan guide) left 'validate-routing' reporting 'OK (42 criteria in sync)' and all ten test_guides.py tests passing.
